Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) allows organizations to train models collaboratively while maintaining data privacy. However, this approach presents significant vulnerabilities to backdoor attacks, which can poison the model during training and manipulate predictions at inference. Recent research reveals that existing defenses do not hold up under realistic conditions, indicating a gap between theoretical findings and practical implementation.

 - Vertical Federated Learning facilitates collaboration without data exposure, creating privacy opportunities.
 - Backdoor attacks pose serious risks, potentially compromising model integrity during both training and inference.
 - Current defenses against these attacks may not be effective in practice, revealing a gap in research and applicability.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12962
